column3: Mouth. It began as a picture of an open mouth, and it brings eating, speaking and sounds. It usually sits on the left, sometimes inside or beneath other parts. Examples: 吃 eat, 喝 drink, 吗 question particle, 哪 which. Many spoken particles such as 吗 and 呢 carry it as the "mouth" clue; in 哥 and 同 it is only part of the shape.

A squeezed form of 人 (person), written on the left side. It marks people and what people do or are. Examples: 你 you, 他 he, 住 live, 做 do, 候 wait. In many of these it is simply the left part, and the sound often comes from the right-hand side.
A squeezed form of 水 (water), written as three drops on the left side. It brings water, liquids and flowing, and also wet or cool states. Examples: 洗 wash, 渴 thirsty, 涼 cool, 淨 clean, 溫 warm.

Tree or wood. It began as a picture of a tree with branches on top and roots below. Left side or bottom, it points to trees and wooden things. Examples: 杯 cup, 桌 table, 校 school, 楼 building. In 東, 果 and 来 it is only part of the shape.
A squeezed form of 手 (hand), written on the left side. It marks actions done with the hands. Examples: 打 hit, 拉 pull, 推 push, 接 receive, 換 change. In 找 and 报 it is just the dictionary radical.

A squeezed form of 辵 (walking), written along the bottom-left and wrapping under the rest. It brings movement, going and distance. Examples: 进 advance, 过 pass, 远 far, 边 side, 送 see off. In 這 it is the sound part, so it can mislead there.
Speech: talking, words and language. It is usually on the left, with 讠 as the form used in simplified characters (the same radical). Examples: 說 speak, 請 please, 謝 thank, 語 language, 認 recognize.
The simplified form of 言 (the same radical), written on the left. It brings speech, words and language. Examples: 说 speak, 请 please, 谢 thank, 语 language, 认 recognize.

Two different radicals share this shape, depending on the side. On the left it comes from 阜 (mound, hill): 院 courtyard, 隊 team. On the right it comes from 邑 (town): 都 all, 部 department, 那 that. Left means hill, right means town, but in many characters it is mostly a shape to file them under.
A squeezed form of 艸 (grass or plant), written across the top. It brings plants, herbs, flowers and food from plants. Examples: 菜 vegetable, 茶 tea, 草 grass, 花 flower, 藥 medicine.

Earth or soil. It began as a picture of a mound of earth. On the left or bottom, it points to ground, places and things built of earth. Examples: 地 ground, 場 field, 墙 wall, 塊 lump. In 坐 and 報 it is only part of the shape.
Heart, mind. It began as a picture of a heart. At the bottom it brings thoughts, feelings and will. Examples: 想 think, 忘 forget, 急 anxious, 意 thought, 思 think. Its squeezed form on the left is 忄.

A squeezed form of 糸 (silk thread), written on the left side. It brings thread, cloth, cords and knots, also colors. Examples: 紅 red, 綠 green, 紙 paper, 給 give, 結 knot. 纟 is the same radical in simplified characters.

A squeezed form of 竹 (bamboo), written across the top. It brings bamboo things, such as 筷 chopsticks and 籃 basket. Much more often it is just a shape to file characters under, not a clue to meaning: 第 order, 答 answer, 等 wait, 算 calculate.

Roof, house. It began as a picture of a house. Written across the top, it brings houses, rooms and shelter. Examples: 家 home, 室 room, 客 guest, 安 peaceful. In 寫 and 定 it is mainly a shape, and in 實 it is the sound part.
The simplified form of 糸 (silk thread), written on the left; the same radical as 糹 in traditional characters. It brings thread, cloth and colors. Examples: 红 red, 绿 green, 纸 paper, 给 give, 结 knot.
A squeezed form of 肉 (meat, flesh), written on the left. It looks like 月 (moon) but brings the body and its parts. Examples: 脑 brain, 脸 face, 腿 leg, 脚 foot, 胖 fat. In 能 it is only a shape.
Woman. It began as a picture of a woman. On the left or bottom, it brings women, family relations and female things. Examples: 妈 mom, 姐 elder sister, 妹 younger sister, 姓 surname, 婚 marry.
Sun, day. It began as a picture of the sun. On the left or top, it brings the sun, daylight and time. Examples: 時 time, 昨 yesterday, 晴 clear weather, 晨 dawn, 星 star. In 是 and 普 it is only a shape.

This is the number one, a single horizontal stroke. As a radical it carries no clue to meaning: 不, 三, 七, 上 and 下 are all filed here only because of the stroke. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.

A squeezed form of 刀 (knife), written on the right side. It brings cutting and sharp things. Examples: 刻 carve, 別 separate, 剧 play. In 到 arrive it is the sound part, and in 前 and 利 it is only a shape.

Enclosure. It is a box drawn around the rest of the character, bringing the idea of surrounding or bounded places. Examples: 国 country, 园 garden, 围 surround, 回 return. In 四, 因 and 图 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.

Cloth, towel. It began as a picture of a hanging piece of cloth. On the left or bottom, it points to cloth things. Examples: 布 cloth, 帶 belt, 幣 currency. In 師, 市 and 希 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
A building with a roof, written over the top-left of a character. It brings houses, shops and rooms. Examples: 店 shop, 床 bed, 座 seat, 庭 courtyard, 廣 wide. In 度, 应 and 平 it is mostly a shape.
A squeezed form of 衣 (clothing), written on the left side. It brings clothes and cloth. Examples: 衫 shirt, 裤 pants, 裙 skirt, 袜 socks, 被 bedding.

In characters this means head. It began as a picture of the head of a kneeling person. Usually on the right. Examples: 頭 head, 顏 face, 領 neck, 顧 look back. By itself it now means page. 页 is the same radical in simplified characters.

A tapping or striking hand, written on the right side. It brings actions done to something. Examples: 教 teach, 放 release, 收 collect, 救 aid, 改 alter. In 整, 散 and 敢 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Eye. It began as a picture of an eye, now turned on its side. On the left or top, it brings the eye and seeing. Examples: 眼 eye, 睛 eyeball, 睡 sleep, 看 look. In 真, 直 and 相 it is mostly a shape.

It began as a picture of a right hand. As a radical it gives no clue to meaning: 友 friend, 难 hard, 发 issue, 受 receive and 反 reverse have nothing in common. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Strength, effort. On the right or bottom it brings strength and work. Examples: 动 move, 助 help, 努 exert, 办 set up, 势 power. In 加 and 功 it is the dictionary radical.
A squeezed form of 心 (heart), written on the left side. It brings feelings, thoughts and states of mind. Examples: 慢 slow, 怕 fear, 情 emotion, 懂 understand, 慣 habit.
Fire. It began as a picture of a fire. On the left it brings fire, heat and burning; at the bottom it is written 灬. Examples: 灯 lamp, 烟 smoke, 烧 burn, 烤 bake, 煩 bother.

A squeezed form of 金 (gold, metal), written on the left side. It brings metal, money and metal objects. Examples: 錢 money, 鐘 clock, 鐵 iron, 銀 silver, 鎖 lock. 钅 is the same radical in simplified characters.

A squeezed form of 火 (fire), written as four dots along the bottom. It brings fire, heat and cooking. Examples: 热 heat, 熟 cooked, 照 shine, 烈 fiery. In 為, 無 and 烏 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Ear. It began as a picture of an ear. On the left or top, it brings hearing and sound. Examples: 聽 hear, 聞 news, 聲 sound, 聰 sharp, 聊 chat.

Shell, money. It began as a picture of a cowrie shell, which was used as money. On the left or bottom, it brings money, trade and value. Examples: 買 buy, 賣 sell, 貴 expensive, 費 expenses, 貨 goods. 贝 is the same radical in simplified characters.

Grain. It began as a picture of a plant stalk. On the left, it brings crops. Examples: 秋 autumn, 租 rent, 種 kind, 積 store up. The link is often loose; in 科 and 称 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Stone. It began as a stone beneath a cliff. On the left, it brings stone and rock, and hard things. Examples: 碗 bowl, 破 break, 碰 touch, 研 grind, 礎 foundation stone.

Big. It began as a picture of a person standing facing forward. As a radical it hardly carries meaning: 太 very, 天 sky, 夫 man, 失 lose. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under, not a clue to meaning.

Person. It began as a side view of a person standing. As a radical it is mostly a shape: 今 modern, 会 meet, 以 by, 从 from, 众 crowd. When the meaning really is person, it is usually written 亻 on the left.
Ice, a compressed form of 仌, written as two dots on the left side. It brings cold. Examples: 冷 cold, 凉 cool, 冰 ice, 净 clean. It has two dots, where the water radical 氵 has three.
Body. It sits over the top-left of a character. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under, not a clue to meaning. Examples: 屋 building, 层 layer, 局 bureau, 尺 ruler, 展 open.
This is the number ten, a cross. As a radical it is not a clue to meaning: 半 half, 午 noon, 南 south and 千 thousand have nothing in common. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.

Field. It began as a picture of a field divided into four sections. As a radical it is mostly a shape: 男 man, 画 picture, 留 stay, 由 cause. Only a few, such as 界 boundary, plausibly have to do with fields.
Child. It began as a picture of a baby. On the left or bottom, it brings children and descendants. Examples: 孩 baby, 孫 grandchild, 學 learning, 字 character. In 季 and 存 it is only part of the shape.

The simplified form of 金 (gold, metal), written on the left; the same radical as 釒 in traditional characters. It brings metal, money and metal objects. Examples: 钱 money, 钟 clock, 铁 iron, 银 silver, 锁 lock.

On the left of a character this is not 王 (king) but a squeezed form of 玉 (jade): written alone, jade has a dot, and as a radical it loses it. It marks jade, gems and fine things. The link shows in 环 ring, bracelet, and in 理, which once meant to cut jade along its grain; in 球 ball and 玩 play it has faded, so there it is mostly a shape to recognize.
A squeezed form of 食 (food, eat), written on the left side, the simplified form of 飠. It brings food and eating. Examples: 饭 meal, 饱 satisfied, 饮 swallow, 饺 dumpling, 饼 rice-cake.

A squeezed form of 食 (food, eat), written on the left side. It brings food and eating. Examples: 飯 meal, 飽 satisfied, 飲 swallow, 餃 dumpling, 餅 rice-cake. 饣 is the same radical in simplified characters.

Short-tailed bird. It began as a picture of a short-tailed bird. On the right, it brings birds, as in 雞 chicken. Elsewhere it is often just a shape to file characters under, or the sound part, as in 雖 although, 隻 only and 雜 mix, so it is not a reliable clue to meaning.

The simplified form of 貝 (shell, money), written on the left or bottom. It brings money, trade and value. Examples: 贵 expensive, 费 expenses, 资 wealth, 货 goods, 赢 win. 貝 is the same radical in traditional characters.

The simplified form of 頁 (head, page), usually on the right. It brings the head and face. Examples: 颜 face, 顺 submit, 领 neck, 顾 look back, 题 forehead. 頁 is the same radical in traditional characters. In 颗 it is the sound part.
Inch. As a radical it is mostly a shape, not a clue to meaning. Examples: 对 correct, 封 envelope, 导 direct, 專 concentrated. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
This is the number eight, two strokes. As a radical it carries no clue to meaning: 六 six, 公 fair, 共 all, 其 his, 具 tool have nothing in common. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.

Child, as a radical placed at the bottom. In 兒 it is the meaning part, but elsewhere it is mostly a shape to file characters under, not a clue to meaning. Examples: 先 first, 元 first, 光 light, 兄 elder brother.

The left half of 行, which represents a street intersection seen from above. Written on the left, it brings walking and going. Examples: 往 go, 從 from, 很 very, 後 after. It looks like 亻 but is unrelated.

It began as a mouth with breath coming out. As a radical it gives no clue to meaning: 書, 會, 最, 更 and 替 are all just filed here. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under. Do not confuse it with 日 (sun).

Spear. It began as an ancient weapon with a single blade. As a radical it is mostly a shape, not a clue to meaning. Examples: 我 I, 或 or, 成 accomplish, 戲 play. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Walk, run. It began as a picture of a running man. On the left or bottom-left, it brings walking, running and going. Examples: 起 start, 超 surpass, 越 exceed, 趕 pursue, 趣 interest.
A single slash stroke. As a radical it carries no clue to meaning: 么, 乐, 久, 义 and 乘 have nothing in common. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.

Silk thread. It began as a picture of a skein of silk. As a radical it brings thread and fibers, though in these characters it is often just a shape. Examples: 紧 tense, 紫 purple, 繁 complex. On the left it is written 纟 (simplified) or 糹 (traditional).
Food, eat. As a radical it brings eating and feeding. Examples: 餐 meal, 養 raise (a family, a pet). It is the full form of 饣 / 飠, which is used on the left side.
A squeezed form of 犬 (dog), written on the left side. It brings animals, especially mammals. Examples: 猫 cat, 狗 dog, 猪 pig, 猴 monkey. A few abstract words have it too, such as 独 alone and 狂 insane.
Sickness. It began as a picture of a person lying in bed, and sits over the top-left of a character. It brings illness and pain. Examples: 病 illness, 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin, 癌 cancer.
Insect, bug. As a radical it brings insects, worms and small creatures, and some other animals. Examples: 蛋 egg, 蛇 snake, 蜂 bee, 蜜 honey, 虹 rainbow. In 虽 it is only a shape.
Cave, hole. It began as a picture of a cave mouth, written across the top. It brings holes, hollows and tight spaces. Examples: 空 empty, 窗 window, 究 investigate, 窮/穷 poor. In 突 it is mostly a shape.

Wine jar. It began as a picture of a wine vessel, and was the original character for 酒 alcohol. At the left it brings alcohol, fermenting and drinks. Examples: 酒 alcohol, 醉 drunk, 醋 vinegar, 酱/醬 sauce, 醒 wake up. Do not confuse it with 西 (west).

Altar. It began as a picture of an altar. As a radical it brings worship and ceremony. Examples: 祭 sacrifice, 禁 forbid. On the left it is written 礻; do not confuse that with 衤 (clothing), which has one more stroke.

A squeezed form of 示 (altar), written on the left side. It brings spirits, worship and good fortune. Examples: 神 god, 祖 ancestor, 福 happiness, 祝 wish, 礼/禮 courtesy. It differs from 衤 (clothing) by one stroke.

Dish, vessel. It began as a picture of an empty container such as a chalice, and sits at the bottom of a character. It brings containers and what they hold. Examples: 盘/盤 tray, 盒 box, 盆 basin, 盛 abundant. In 盐 salt and 益 benefit it is only a shape.

Cliff. A stroke that sits over the top-left of a character and covers it. Examples: 原 source, 厨 kitchen, 厅 hall, 厚 thick. In 压 and 历 it is mostly a shape. Do not confuse it with 广, which has an extra dot on top.
Two strokes on top of a character, a top form of 八 (eight). It brings no clue to meaning and is mostly a shape to file characters under. Examples: 关 close, 单 single, 养 raise, 兰 orchid.
A net, written across the top; the top form of 网 (net). It brings nets and covering. Examples: 罵 scold, 置 place, 署 office, 罩 cover. In 罪 sin and 罢 stop it is mostly a shape.
Feather, wings. It began as a picture of wings or feathers. It brings feathers, wings and flight. Examples: 翅 wing, 翼 wing, 翔 soar, 翠 emerald. In 習 practice it is mostly a shape.
A hand holding a tool or weapon, written on the right side. It brings striking and force. Examples: 殺 kill, 殴/毆 beat, 毅 resolute. In 段 and 殿 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
A tiger's head, the top form of 虎 (tiger), written across the top. As a radical it is mostly a shape. Examples: 虚/虛 empty, 虐 cruel, 虧 lose. In 處 place and 虏/虜 captive it is the sound part.
Bitter, hardship. It is mostly a shape to file characters under. Examples: 辣 spicy, 辩/辯 argue, 辭 words. In 辦 handle it is the sound part. One way to see it: a hot iron used to brand prisoners.

Lid, a cover with a handle on top. Rare as a radical; it gives no clue to meaning, and in many characters it stands for something else, such as the roof of a tower in 高, 京, 亭 and 亮. Examples: 京 capital, 亮 bright, 交 meet, 亡 die.
A kneeling person seen from the side. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 却 but, 印 print, 即 at once. In 卸 unload it is the sound part.
Corpse, death. It began as a picture of human remains. It brings death, injury and badness. Examples: 死 die, 殘/残 injure, 殖 breed, 殃 misfortune.
Small table. It began as a picture of a small stool seen from the side. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 凳 bench, 凡 ordinary, 凯/凱 triumphant.

Scholar, soldier. It began as a picture of a war axe, and later came to mean soldier and scholar. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 壮/壯 strong, 声 sound, 壶/壺 jar. Do not confuse it with 土 (earth): 士 has the longer top line, 土 the longer bottom line.
Evening. It began as a picture of a crescent moon. Rare as a radical; it hints at night and time, though 多 much and 外 outside are mostly a shape. Examples: 夜 night, 夢 dream, 够/夠 enough.
Arrow. It began as a picture of an arrow. On the left it brings short or straight things. Examples: 短 short, 矮 short (of height), 矩 square, 矫/矯 straighten. In 知 know it is the sound part.
A single vertical stroke. As a radical it carries no clue to meaning and is mostly a shape to file characters under. Examples: 中 middle, 个 piece, 书 book, 串 string.
An open box, a container with the top open. Rare as a radical; it carries no clue to meaning in these characters and is mostly a shape. Examples: 出 go out, 凶 fierce, 凹 concave, 凸 convex.
Wrap. It began as a picture of a person bending over, and sits over the top-left of a character. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 包 wrap, 勺 spoon, 勿 do not, 匆 hurried.
Leather. It began as a picture of a stretched animal hide. On the left it brings leather and things made of it. Examples: 鞋 shoe, 靴 boot, 鞭 whip, 靶 target.
A single dot. As a radical it carries no clue to meaning and is mostly a shape to file characters under. Examples: 主 master, 为 do, 丸 ball, 丹 red.
Cover. A cloth for covering things, written across the top. Rare as a radical; it carries no clue to meaning and is mostly a shape. Examples: 写 write, 农 farming, 冠 crown, 冤 wrong.
Hiding enclosure, a box open on one side. Rare as a radical, and easily mistaken for 匚. Examples: 区/區 area, 匹 measure word for horses, 匿 hide.
Lame. It shows a man with bent legs. Rare as a radical; the characters 尴/尷 and 尬 (both "embarrassed") carry it as their meaning part. Examples: 就 then, 尤 especially, 尴/尷 awkward.
Work, tool. It began as a picture of a bladed tool. Rare as a radical in everyday characters, mostly a shape. Examples: 左 left, 差 differ, 巧 skillful.
Two hands side by side. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 开 open, 弄 do, 弃 abandon, 异 different.
Snout. In many characters it actually shows a hand holding something. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 录 record, 归 return, 寻 seek.
Hair, decoration: three strokes written on the right, like tufts of hair or rays of light. It brings decoration, color and light. Examples: 影 shadow, 彩 color, 形 shape, 彰 reveal.
Claw. It began as a picture of a hand grabbing from above, and is written across the top. Rare as a radical in everyday characters. Examples: 爬 climb, 爪 claw.
Body. It began as a picture of a pregnant woman. On the left it brings the body and its posture. Examples: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躬 bow, 躯/軀 body.
A wide frame, open at the bottom; a border or a territory. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 再 again, 冒 risk, 册/冊 volume, 冈 ridge. Do not confuse it with 囗, a closed box.
Divination. Perhaps a picture of a crack in an oracle bone used for divination. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 卡 card, 卦 divination sign.
Tiny. It began as a picture of a short silk thread; compare 糸. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 幼 young, 幻 illusion, 幽 secluded, 乡 country.
Father. It began as a hand holding a stone axe. It brings fathers and older men. Examples: 爸 dad, 爷/爺 grandfather, 爹 dad, 父 father.
Bean. It began as a picture of a kind of container, and the word was later borrowed for the plant. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 豆 bean, 豐 abundant, 豈 how could, 豔 gorgeous.
Long hair, written across the top. It brings hair and beards. Examples: 髮 hair, 鬚 beard, 髦 fashionable.
A hook, a vertical stroke ending in a hook. As a radical it carries no clue to meaning and is mostly a shape to file characters under. Examples: 了 finished, 事 matter, 争 dispute, 予 give.
Box. It began as a picture of a container, written as an open frame. Rare as a radical; it brings boxes and containers. Examples: 匠 craftsman, 巨 huge, 匪 bandit. Easily mixed up with 匸.
Private. It was the original form of 私 (private). Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 去 go, 参/參 join, 县 county.
Go. It began as a picture of a downward footprint, written across the top. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 备 prepare, 处 place, 务 affairs. 夊 is a close variant.
River: three flowing strokes. Rare as a radical in everyday characters. Examples: 巡 patrol, 巢 nest.
Self. It began as a picture of a silk rope for binding things. Rare as a radical; it is easily confused with 已 (already) and 巳. Examples: 己 self, 已 already.
Shield, dry. It began as a picture of a shield with ornaments on top. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 年 year, 幸 fortunate, 幹/干 do, 并 combine.
Dipper, measure. It began as a picture of a dipper held by a hand, used for measuring grain. On the right it brings measuring and pouring. Examples: 料 material, 斜 slanted, 斗 dipper.
Air, steam. Rare as a radical, but it brings gas and air. Examples: 氧 oxygen, 氛 atmosphere, 气/氣 air.
Brush. It began as a hand holding a writing brush. Rare as a radical in everyday characters; mostly a shape. Examples: 肆 reckless, 肇 begin.

Minister, official. It began as a picture of an eye looking down, and that sense shows in 臨 look down and 監/监 supervise. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 臣 minister, 卧/臥 lie down, 臨 draw near.
Mortar, a bowl for grinding grain. Rare as a radical in everyday characters; mostly a shape. Examples: 興 prosper, 與 and, 舊 old, 舅 uncle.
Pig. It began as a picture of a pig. On the left it brings pigs and some other animals. Examples: 豬 pig (猪 in simplified, with 犭), 象 elephant, 豪 brave.
Teeth. It began as a picture of a mouth full of teeth, with a part for the sound added. On the left it brings teeth and age. Examples: 龄/齡 age, 齿/齒 teeth.
Spoon. It began as a picture of a spoon. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 北 north, 化 change, 匙 spoon.
A long stride; a man with one leg behind him. Written at the bottom-left, wrapping under the rest. Rare as a radical; it brings walking and building. Examples: 建 build, 延 extend, 廷 court.
Do not. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. It is the same as 母 (mother) with the two dots joined into one stroke.
Clan, family. Rare as a radical; only 氏 itself is in the lists, so it is mostly met in dictionaries.
Sweet. A tongue or something sweet in an open mouth. Rare as a radical; in these characters it shows taste. Examples: 甜 sweet, 甘 sweet, 甚 very.
Earthen jar. It began as a picture of an earthenware jar with a lid. On the left it brings jars and pottery. Examples: 缸 vat, 罐 jar, 缺 lack.
Cover; the top form of 襾. Rare as a radical in everyday characters; mostly a shape. Examples: 要 want, 覆 cover.
A legless beast, a form of an animal. Rare as a radical; it brings animals. Examples: 貓 cat (猫 in simplified, with 犭), 豹 leopard, 貌 appearance.
Morning. It possibly began as a picture of a farming tool. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 農 farming, 辱 insult, 辰 morning.
Distinguish. It began as a picture of an animal paw with spread toes. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 采 pick, 释/釋 explain.
Fight. It began as a picture of two figures facing each other and fighting. Rare as a radical. Examples: 鬧 noisy, 鬥 fight, 鬨 boisterous.
Salt. It began as a picture of a bag of salt. Rare as a radical. Examples: 鹽 salt, 鹹 salty, 卤 brine.
Go slowly. A footprint pointing down, a variant of 夂. Written at the bottom of a character. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 夏 summer, 复 again.
Without, no. A simplified form of 無 (the same word), also used in older writing. Rare as a radical. Example: 无 no.
Crisscross: two stacked X marks. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 爾 you, 爽 crisp.
The side form of 爿 (half of a tree trunk), written on the left. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Examples: 牆 wall, 将 will.
Bolt of cloth. It began as a picture of a foot with a leg on top. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 疑 doubt, 疏 sparse.
Footsteps: two feet pointing apart, written across the top. Rare as a radical. Examples: 登 climb, 發 issue.
Track, footprint. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Examples: 离 leave, 禽 birds.
Plow. It began as a picture of a wooden plow. It brings plowing and farming. Examples: 耕 plow, 耗 consume.
Stopping, tough. A person looking back. Rare as a radical; mostly a shape. Examples: 良 good, 艱 difficult.
Valley. It began as a picture of a valley between two mountain walls. Rare as a radical in everyday characters. Examples: 谷 valley, 豁 open.
Red. Fire and a person: the color of fire. Rare as a radical in everyday characters. Examples: 赤 red, 赫 bright.
Servant. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Example: 隶/隸 servant.
Tanned leather. 韋 is the traditional form. Rare as a radical in everyday characters. Examples: 韧/韌 tough.
Millet. It began as a picture of a cereal grain. Rare as a radical in everyday characters. Examples: 黎 many, 黏 sticky.
Sprout. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Example: 屯 village.
Tethered arrow. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Example: 式 style.
Spear. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Example: 矛 spear.
Oppose. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Example: 舞 dance.
Sacrificial wine. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Example: 鬱 gloomy.
Cauldron. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Example: 融 melt.
Tripod vessel. It began as a picture of an ancient bronze vessel with three legs. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries. Example: 鼎 cauldron.
City. On the right it is written 阝. Rare as a radical in its full form; it is mostly met in dictionaries.
Leek. It began as a picture of a leek growing in the ground. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries.
Embroidery, needlework. Rare as a radical; no character of the everyday lists has it, so it is mostly met in dictionaries.
Frog. It began as a picture of a frog. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries.
Flute. It began as a picture of a bamboo pan flute. Rare as a radical; mostly met in dictionaries.
A form of 水 (water) written at the bottom of a character. Rare as a radical; in most characters it is now only a shape. Examples: 泰 peaceful, 求 seek, 录 record, 屬 belong.
A squeezed form of 長 (long). It is the left half of 髟 (long hair), so it sits on top of 髮 hair and 鬆 loose; it is also in 肆 wanton and at the bottom of 套 cover.

Choke. It began as a picture of a kneeling figure turned around with its mouth open; 欠 shows one facing forward. Rare as a radical: mostly met on the right of 既 already, and through it in 概 general and 慨 sigh.
Claw: the form 爪 takes when written across the top of a character. In 受 receive and 采 pick it is a hand taking hold. Other examples: 爭 strive, 愛 love, 為 do.

Tap, knock lightly. It began as a hand 又 holding a stick or tool, whose top later came to look like 卜. The full form of 攵: most characters write it as 攵 on the right (教 teach, 放 release); 敲 knock keeps 攴.
Snout, the same radical as 彐 in another shape. Rare; mostly a shape. Example: 彙 collect.
Cover. In characters it is written in its top form 覀: 要 want, 票 ticket, 覆 cover. 西 west looks much the same but is a character of its own.

Mound, hill. It began as a picture of a row of steps up a hill. On the left of a character it is squeezed into 阝: 院 courtyard, 陽 sun, 隊 team. On its own it is rare, mostly in names such as 曲阜, the hometown of Confucius.
